title: Local pullback preserves a specified bottom homology isomorphism
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $a\in\mathbf Z$, $M$ an $\mathcal O_T$-module sheaf, and $f:M[-a]\to D$ an arrow inducing an isomorphism on $H^a$. Choose derived categories for all schemes in one localization universe. Let $U\subset T$ be open, and let $K$ be a bounded-above cochain complex on $U$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with finite free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module], zero in every degree below $a$, and with $d^a=0$. Fix $e:L(U\hookrightarrow T)^*D\cong Q(K)$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. For any morphism $g:T\prime\to T$ and point $y\in T\prime$ such that $g(y)\in U$, there exists an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ such that the restriction to $V$ of the module-sheaf map $H^a(Lg^*f)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Pullback clause, computed using 06YD/06YJ, composition 0D5S, and affine chain representatives as in 08CR second proof

proof.text: Exact open restriction and e identify H^a(D)|U with H^a(K). The zero bottom differentials identify H^a(K) with K^a. The isomorphism on H^a(f) therefore identifies M|U with the finite free sheaf K^a. Refine U by affine opens and transport restrictions to their localized sites.

The single complex on M and K restricted to an affine refinement are strictly perfect, since K is bounded above and zero below a. Represent the conjugated restricted arrow f by a chain map alpha using the affine perfect-map representative theorem. Both short complexes at a have zero differentials. HomologyData.ofZeros and its map naturality identify H^a(alpha) with alpha.f a. The hypothesis on H^a(f) and exact restriction make alpha.f a invertible.

Finite free terms are flat and the complexes are bounded above. Compute their pullback along the inverse-image chart by the natural flat-complex counit. Its naturality computes the pullback of this specified chain map. Termwise pullback preserves zero objects, zero maps and invertible components. Its bottom homology map is therefore invertible. Derived composition and exact open restriction identify it with H^a(Lg*f) restricted to the inverse image of the affine chart containing g(y). This inverse image contains y, giving V. The arrow is fixed globally, so no compatibility of unrelated local object isomorphisms is required.

theorem zeroBottomArrow_pullback_local
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (D : schemeDerivedCategory T) (a : ℤ)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace))
    (f : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) a).obj M ⟶ D)
    (hf : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) a).map f))
    (U : T.Opens)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ c : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, c < i → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hnegative : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hzero : K.d a (a + 1) = 0)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (K.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin n))))
    (e : (derivedPullback U.ι).obj D ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)
    (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T' ⟶ T) (y : T') (hy : g.base y ∈ U) :
    ∃ V : T'.Opens, y ∈ V ∧
      IsIso (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T'.toRingedSpace)) a).map
          ((derivedPullback g).map f)).over V)
